goal: Send members a reminder when a borrowed tool is overdue.

constraints.summary: The host runs one cron job a day at 06:00, with no queue or long-running worker.
The mail relay accepts at most 50 messages an hour and rejects the rest with a 451.
Each member chose email, sms, or none, and nothing in the project sends SMS.
Due dates are calendar days in the library's time zone, America/Denver.

questions.question: cadence
questions.summary: When the first reminder goes out and how often it repeats is a policy that no file in the project sets down.
questions.answer: Send the first reminder the day after the due date, then one every three days until the tool is back.

questions.question: sms-members
questions.summary: Members who chose SMS cannot be reached by any sender the project has.
questions.answer: Email only. Members who chose text messages or no contact get no reminder.

questions.question: over-limit
questions.summary: More reminders may be due in one run than the relay accepts in an hour.
questions.answer: Cap each run at what the relay accepts, oldest loans first, and leave the rest for the next run.

questions.question: path
questions.summary: Step 5 of Work it out asks where to write the file.

needless.question: mail-sender
needless.summary: toolshed/mail.py already sends email through the relay.

needless.question: contact-store
needless.summary: data/members.csv has each member's email address and contact preference.

needless.question: time-zone
needless.summary: LIBRARY_TZ sets the time zone of due dates.

needless.question: scheduler
needless.summary: ops/crontab runs one job a day, and there is no queue or worker.
